narrative:
Your loan application was reviewed by our credit assessment system, which evaluated your financial profile and determined a predicted likelihood of bad credit at 51% — just above the threshold required for approval. While this is a borderline result, it was enough to result in a denial, and understanding the specific factors behind this decision may help you take steps to strengthen a future application.

The single most influential factor working against your application was the current status of your checking account, which shows a negative balance. Among applicants who were approved, nearly half had no checking account at all, and the majority of the rest maintained positive balances. A negative checking account balance is a strong signal of financial strain, and it weighed most heavily in the model's assessment of your situation.

The second most important factor was your credit history. Your record shows no prior credits or all credits fully paid — which might sound positive, but in practice, it means there is very little evidence of how you manage ongoing debt obligations over time. Approved applicants overwhelmingly had a history of existing credits that were being paid on time, or even some past difficulties that had since been resolved. The absence of a meaningful credit track record makes it harder for the system to assess your reliability as a borrower, and this uncertainty pushed the prediction toward risk.

On a more positive note, your property ownership — specifically your real estate — actually worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward approval. This is a meaningful asset that the model recognized as a stabilizing factor in your financial profile, and it is one of the reasons your predicted risk sits so close to the borderline.

Beyond these top three factors, your overall profile has several encouraging elements: your requested loan amount of 1,108 DM is well below the average of nearly 2,887 DM among approved applicants, your loan duration of 12 months is shorter than average, and you have stable employment of 4 to 7 years in a skilled position. These details suggest you are not overextending yourself financially.

To improve your chances in a future application, the most impactful steps would be to bring your checking account into a positive balance and, if possible, establish a clearer credit history by responsibly managing a smaller credit product beforehand. You may also consider speaking with a bank advisor who can review your full financial situation and potentially identify additional ways to strengthen your application.
